texts.preamble: Eshwar Roa vs Commissioner, Bbmp on 16 August, 2025 Kabc010165122024 In The Court Of The Iii Addl. City Civil And Sessions Judge, (Cch-25) At Bengaluru. Dated: This The 16th Day Of August, 2025 Present : Smt. Nisharani A.C., B.A., Ll.B., Iii Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru. O.S.No.4507/2024 Plaintiff : Sri.Eshwar Rao S/o Venkob Rao, Aged about 45 years, R/at No.7/3 B, No.8 Ground floor, 1st Cross, Abbigere, Bengaluru - 560 090. (By Sri.Shankaraiah B., Advocate) V/S Defendants : 1. Commissioner Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike, Hudson Circle, Bengaluru-560 002. 2. Assistant Revenue Officer Shettihalli Sub Division, Bbmp Ward No.12, Near Govt. School, Ravindranagar, Bengaluru -560 015. (By Sri.K.R.R., Advocate) 2 O.S.No.4507/2024 Judgment On Preliminary Issue Additional Issue No.1
texts.facts: This suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants for permanent injunction and such other consequential reliefs. Schedule Property: All that piece and parcel of the shop bearing Eshwar Roa vs Commissioner, Bbmp on 16 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146635859/ 1 No.1, "Ganesh Fast Food" situated at Abbigere, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru, measuring East to West 10 feet and North to South 12 feet, in all measuring 120 sq.ft., RCC roof building and bounded on:- East by : Shop No.2, West by : BBMP Property, North by : Road, South by : Vacant land. 2. The brief facts of the Plaintiff's case is as under:- The plaintiff is the tenant under the ownership of Abbigere Municipality on a monthly rent of Rs.1,000/- and carrying a hotel business under the name and style "Ganesh Fast Food" and he has taken general license/ 3 O.S.No.4507/2024 permission to run the hotel from the president Abbigere Village Panchayath, Bengaluru North on 18.12.2006. He is regularly paying rent to Abbigere Municipality and now it is comes under the BBMP. The plaintiff has also paid 2 months rent to BBMP on October 2009 for a sum of Rs.2,000/- and also paid Rs.5,000/- vide receipt dated 18.07.2023. The defendant No.2 refused to receive the rent as such the plaintiff was forced to send the total rent for a sum of Rs.12,000/- to the defendant No.1 by way of demand draft bearing No.323213 dated 19.06.2024 drawn on Canara Bank, Chikkabanavara, Bengaluru. The defendant No.2 had issued a notice dated 27.05.2024, calling upon the plaintiff to pay the rent and hand over possession of the suit schedule premises within 15 days. Eshwar Roa vs Commissioner, Bbmp on 16 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146635859/ 2 The plaintiff has sent request letter dated 14.06.2024, requesting the defendant No.2 to renew his tenancy in respect of the suit schedule property. If the defendants not restrained by granting an order of permanent injunction, the plaintiff will be put to great injustice, loss and mental agony, on the other hand defendants will not be put to any 4 O.S.No.4507/2024 hardship. The cause of action for the suit arose on 27.05.2024 when the defendant No.2 caused notice demanding the plaintiff to handover vacant possession of the suit schedule property. Hence, filed this suit. 3. The defendants appeared before the court through their counsel and filed written statement stating that the suit filed by the plaintiff in respect of schedule property is wholly false, frivolous and vexatious and same is not maintainable either in law or on facts. The suit has been filed with an intention to harass the defendants and to coerce them to terms. The plaintiff has suppressed all the real facts and mis-represented the same before this Court. The plaintiff has not issued the statutory notice as required under Sec.482 of KMC Act or Sec.80(2) of CPC before filing the suit. The defendants are denies the entire allegations made in the plaint and stated that the plaintiff is illegally occupied the suit schedule premises without obtaining the valid permission to run the shop from the BBMP authority and not entered the rental agreement with the BBMP and this is Eshwar Roa vs Commissioner, Bbmp on 16 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146635859/ 3 5 O.S.No.4507/2024 against the provisions of BBMP Act 2020 as a result, the BBMP has directed the plaintiff to vacate the suit schedule premises and hand over the possession to the BBMP. As it is a property of BBMP following due process of law in the first instance has issued notice to the plaintiff on 27.05.2024, calling upon the plaintiff to pay the rent and hand over the possession of the suit schedule premises within 15 days. Hence, prayed to dismiss the suit with exemplary costs. 4. Based on the said pleadings this Court framed as many as four Issues and one additional issue and among them Additional Issue No.1 is treated as preliminary issue.
